H01.note: Converged on the full namespace: a client that serves `trace_*` implements all nine methods, with no optional subset or discovery mechanism. Erigon, Nethermind and Reth expose all nine, and so does the Geth draft fork; Besu lacks only individual replay, `trace_replayTransaction`; a Besu maintainer called adding it a good suggestion on #11357, and Besu #11406 implements it. A method a client does not serve still returns -32601, never an empty result. This records direction from implementations, not unanimous formal approval.

besu.note: Justin Florentine called adding trace_replayTransaction a good suggestion and asked Usman Saleem for input; Besu #11406 implements it.

H02.note: Converged on a single traceAddress path returning one object or null. Besu and Erigon development builds already select by tree path, and Reth merged the path lookup in #27366 (2026-09-22). Nethermind still returns a collection and has not stated a position. This records direction from implementations, not unanimous formal approval.

sources.label: Reth #27366: select trace_get results by tree path

H03.note: Converged on direction: AND by default, retaining explicit union and intersection and rejecting unknown modes. This records direction, not unanimous formal approval or implementation uptake. Document the migration for both-lists/no-mode queries.

erigon.note: Agrees with AND by default and rejecting unknown modes, provided an explicit `mode: "intersection"` stays valid as a no-op and `mode: "union"` remains for migrating queries that supply both lists.

H04.note: Every development build treats an omitted, null or empty address list as no restriction: Besu and the Geth draft already did, and Erigon (#24255) and Nethermind (#13857) merged the change. Reth takes it through Alloy #4257, merged but not yet in an Alloy release that Reth ships. This records direction from implementations, not unanimous formal approval.

H05.note: Erigon, Nethermind, Reth and the Geth draft emit no synthetic reward on a PoS block and no records for genesis, after merged fixes in each (Erigon #24295, Nethermind #13783/#13801/#13938, Reth #27423 with Alloy #4218). Besu still differs, with no submitted fix. This records direction from implementations, not unanimous formal approval.

H06.note: Converged on null for a missing transaction or trace path: Reth and Erigon support it, Nethermind merged its alignment (#13937), matching Parity, eth_getTransactionByHash in every client, and the current behavior of Erigon, Reth and Besu (Besu for trace_get). Errors stay for what cannot be answered: pruned history returns an error, never a fake absence, and a bad range is an error (-32602 recommended). An unknown selected block errors (-32001 recommended); Erigon’s question whether it should also be null was answered on #890, and trace_replayBlockTransactions follows trace_block. This records direction from implementations and client teams, not unanimous formal approval.

nethermind.note: Merged #13937, which returns null for a missing transaction as the draft does; its reviewer had preferred not-found errors, and the merge records agreement.

reth.note: Keep null for hash-based lookups: the least bad response, already what most clients return, and it introduces no new behavior for applications to handle.

erigon.note: Trace methods should answer as eth_* does: null for a missing entity (transaction, trace path, and it argues an unknown selected block too), [] for a query that matched nothing, -32602 for a bad range, and an error for pruned history, never a fake absence. Its pruned-history refusals exist but surface as generic -32000.

H07.note: Converged on carrying transactionHash in individual and block replay envelopes. Erigon and Nethermind development builds already include it, and Reth merged #27365 (2026-09-22). Besu is partial. This records direction from implementations, not unanimous formal approval.

sources.label: Reth #27365: include transaction hash in individual replays

H08.note: Erigon, Nethermind (#13667), Reth and the Geth draft keep the stable envelope: output is the return bytes, trace is [] and stateDiff/vmTrace are null when not requested, and the tracer selection never changes the output. Besu is only partially assessed. This records direction from implementations, not unanimous formal approval.

H09.note: Converged on the failed-frame format, including a reverted CREATE reporting {gasUsed, output} with error "Reverted" and no address or code, as a reverted CALL does. Erigon proposed the same shape on execution-apis#890 after the heads-up, the Erigon and Nethermind development builds implement it (#24355, #24356; #13981), and revm-inspectors #533 implements it, released in 0.44.1, which the Anvil nightly ships and Reth does not pin yet. Parity’s failure labels, with the listed extensions, are part of the same fixes. This records direction from implementations and client teams, not unanimous formal approval.

erigon.note: Proposes the draft’s reverted-CREATE shape itself: result {gasUsed, output} with error "Reverted", as a reverted CALL, since the error field already signals failure and EIP-211 fills the return-data buffer only when a create reverts. Success keeps {address, code, gasUsed}; other halts have a null result and the halt message.

H10.note: Erigon, Nethermind and Reth agree on creation results and call actions in both builds. Besu reports deployed bytecode under `output` and omits `creationMethod` from most create frames; its open #11362 covers the self-destructing creation case only. This records direction from implementations, not unanimous formal approval.

sources.label: Besu #11362: report empty code for self-destructing creations

H11.note: Erigon, Nethermind (#13667), Reth and the Geth draft accept an empty trace-type selection, execute the call and return its output. Besu still differs, with no submitted fix. This records direction from implementations, not unanimous formal approval.

H12.note: Every build runs two-argument trace_rawTransaction against latest state in the head block environment, so the baseline is settled. The optional third block selector is an extension: Reth and Anvil honor it (the selected block’s post-state and header; pending uses the next-block environment over latest), and Erigon, Nethermind, Besu and the Geth draft reject it with -32602. No client ignores it. This records direction from implementations, not unanimous formal approval.

H13.note: Converged on strict execution validation, including nonce, balance and sender-code checks. Error codes are recommended, not required (2026-09-29): the eth_sendRawTransaction groups with the -32003 fallback, so a rejection agrees when it names its own violation. Erigon’s development build and Reth agree; Besu differs in behavior, and compatibility migration remains open. Nethermind explicitly supports block-inclusion validation for trace_rawTransaction and permissive eth_call-like trace_call (2026-09-30), and its development build implements it (#14091, captured 2026-10-01).

erigon.note: Agrees, widened to the full admission rules at the selected state: nonce, balance and EIP-3607. Asks that the error code be settled with the policy (Erigon rejects with -32000, Reth with -32000/-32003), and notes that the check interacts with any restored blockNumber field.

nethermind.note: Supports strict trace_rawTransaction validation with the same checks as block inclusion; trace_call remains permissive like eth_call. This does not approve every fee default in H15 or claim implementation uptake.

H14.note: Converged on the core parameter and rejection direction: malformed input and conflicting data/input are rejected, equal calldata values are accepted, and validation errors name the actual violation. Erigon agrees with the direction; Nethermind explicitly supports the calldata rule and prefers one error map shared by all methods (2026-09-30). The shared-map preference is recorded without treating it as approval of every recommended numeric code or every H14 clause. Codes remain recommended, implementation differences remain, and this is direction aligned rather than unanimous formal approval.

erigon.note: Agrees with the direction. Erigon already maps the eth_simulateV1 codes but only that method uses them; the trace paths still need the -32003 fallback, -32602 for malformed input and unknown-field rejection in filter requests.

nethermind.note: Supports rejecting unequal data/input everywhere with -32602, matching Geth, while accepting equal values. Prefers one shared error map so the same failure gets the same code across methods. The comment does not endorse every H14 clause or settle the full numeric map; the draft still recommends codes rather than requiring them.

H15.note: Converged: ordinary execution fees follow eth_call (omitted fees are 0; a zero effective price runs with GASPRICE and BASEFEE 0 and no fee effects; priced calls are validated and charged), blob calls without a positive maxFeePerBlobGas run with BLOBBASEFEE 0 (Erigon’s rule), and an explicit gas of 0 is a zero limit. Erigon agreed on execution-apis#890 and shipped it; Nethermind merged its alignment (#14045, #14046, #14092), which counts as agreement. Remaining gaps are implementation: Reth’s disable_fee_charge question (paradigmxyz/reth#27476) and Besu’s open #11404. This records direction from implementations and client teams, not unanimous formal approval.

erigon.note: Agrees and has shipped the ordinary fee rules: omitted fees default to 0, a zero effective price runs with GASPRICE and BASEFEE 0 and no fee balance effects, validation is skipped only when both caps are 0, and a priced call pays upfront gas, refunds, burn and tip. Proposed the blob rule H15 adopted: each fee is decided independently, BASEFEE zeroed at a zero execution price and BLOBBASEFEE zeroed for a blob call (blobVersionedHashes or maxFeePerBlobGas present) whose maxFeePerBlobGas is not positive. Will fix its trace_callMany, which recognizes the configuration wrapper but never applies its state overrides. Asked whether an explicit gas: 0 means omitted, asking only that eth_call and trace_call agree; H15 answered on 2026-10-01 that it is a zero limit, rejected (-38013 recommended), which needs Erigon to drop the zero fallback in its eth_call family. Erigon has not replied to that yet.

nethermind.note: Merged the H15 alignment: zero-fee calls see BASEFEE 0 (#14045), tip-above-cap precedence (#14046) and the blob-fee rule for eth_call and trace calls (#14092).

H16.note: Converged on implementation evidence: a transaction’s stateDiff reports its fee payments, block-level balance changes stay out of transaction diffs, and each trace_callMany item is a separate transaction that starts fresh per-transaction scopes (original storage, access sets, transient storage, refunds) from the preceding item’s post-state in one shared block environment; a failing item returns one error, with error.data.index recommended. Reth’s development build agrees on every case and Nethermind, Erigon (after merged #24328) and the Geth draft agree on every assessable case; Besu has #11365 open. This records direction from implementations and client teams, not unanimous formal approval.

erigon.note: Merged its H16 alignment (#24328), which counts as agreement.

H17.note: Erigon, Nethermind and Reth development builds agree on created and deleted account markers (Nethermind #13668, revm-inspectors #526, shipped in Reth 2.7.0). Besu is only partially assessed: some state-diff requests return errors, and no checked case differs. This records direction from implementations, not unanimous formal approval.

sources.label: Nethermind #13668: serialize deleted account fields with deletion markers
revm-inspectors #526: preserve account existence in state diffs

H18.note: Converged on reporting net EIP-7702 code changes in stateDiff. Erigon and Nethermind development builds already do, and revm-inspectors merged #509 (2026-09-15); Reth 2.7.0 ships it with revm-inspectors 0.44.0. Besu is partial, and multi-authorization cases remain untested. This records direction from implementations, not unanimous formal approval.

sources.label: revm-inspectors #509: report EIP-7702 code changes in state diffs

H19.note: Erigon, Nethermind and Reth development builds agree that a vmTrace frame holds the executed bytecode (Reth #27213 with revm-inspectors #511, shipped in 2.7.0). Besu is only partially assessed: some vmTrace requests return errors, and no checked case differs. This records direction from implementations, not unanimous formal approval.

sources.label: revm-inspectors #511: record executed bytecode in VM traces
Reth #27213: populate VM bytecode in block replay traces

H20.note: Converged on the vmTrace step rules as revised by the divergent-decisions review: operand-range mem (the full CALL output window preferred, the copied bytes accepted), no synthetic operations, halted operations kept with ex: null. Erigon confirmed its own behavior already matches except what erigontech/erigon#24344 fixes; Nethermind’s development build agrees since #13940 and #13958, and revm-inspectors #532, released in 0.44.1, brings the Anvil nightly into agreement on the checked cases; Reth does not pin 0.44.1 yet. This records direction from implementations and client teams, not unanimous formal approval.

erigon.note: The operand-range mem rule matches Erigon already: MLOAD records the 32-byte range at its operand offset after the operation, and a call records the full declared output window. Its remaining difference is what #24344 addresses.

H21.note: Nethermind and Reth development builds agree on vmTrace number encoding (Nethermind #13750 and #13780). Besu and Erigon are only partially assessed: some vmTrace requests return errors, and no checked case differs. This records direction from implementations, not unanimous formal approval.

sources.label: Nethermind #13750: serialize Parity VM stack values as quantities
Nethermind #13780: serialize vmTrace store key and value as quantities

H22.note: Erigon, Nethermind and Reth report a successful precompile frame's output in both builds. Besu drops it; #11346 is open. This records direction from implementations, not unanimous formal approval.

sources.label: Besu #11346: retain precompile output in Parity call frames

H23.note: Converged on matching a record only by the addresses it reports: a failed CREATE has no created-address match because its result carries no address (H09). Erigon agrees and its development build implements it (#24355); revm-inspectors #533 implements it for Reth and Anvil, released in 0.44.1. Nethermind’s development build drops the address from the reverted CREATE result (#13981), but its trace_filter still matches the would-be address through the internal `action.To`. This records direction from implementations and client teams, not unanimous formal approval.

erigon.note: A reverted CREATE reports no would-be address, so trace_filter has nothing to match it by; the error field still marks the failure.

H24.note: Erigon, Nethermind and Reth keep a failure local to its own frame in both builds. Besu can mark other frames failed; #11345 is open. This records direction from implementations, not unanimous formal approval.

sources.label: Besu #11345: keep Parity trace failures local to their call frame

H25.note: Erigon and Reth report a failure found before output as one complete JSON-RPC error. Nethermind can leave truncated JSON on the wire for a rejected signed transaction; #13666 fixes it and has both reviewers' approval. Besu nests a complete error envelope inside a trace_callMany result, with no submitted fix. This records direction from implementations, not unanimous formal approval.

sources.label: Nethermind #13666: preserve error responses for streamed traces

H26.note: Converged on fork-correct deletion markers: pre-Cancun SELFDESTRUCT deletes the account, post-Cancun it deletes only accounts created in the same transaction. Besu and Erigon development builds agree; Nethermind merged #13668 (2026-09-24, in the captured development build) and revm-inspectors merged #510 (2026-09-15), which Reth 2.7.0 ships with revm-inspectors 0.44.0. The storage of a deleted account is {} under the revised recommendation. This records direction from implementations, not unanimous formal approval.

sources.label: Nethermind #13668: serialize deleted account fields with deletion markers

H27.note: Erigon and Nethermind return the same records for a range filter across a fork boundary as for the concatenated per-block traces. Besu's range filter differs, and its block replay skips pre-block system calls; #10953 is open. Reth is only partially assessed because one per-block reference request returns an error. This records direction from implementations, not unanimous formal approval.

sources.label: Besu #10953: replay block pre-execution before tracing transactions

H28.note: Historical trace_call agrees on every captured native build, including Erigon 3.7.0, which ships the end-of-block history boundary from #24056 (merged 2026-09-18). Two differences remain outside trace_call, both captured and both with an open fix. Besu block replay skips the block’s pre-block system calls, so the mined beacon-root and history reads see the parent’s values (Besu #10953). Erigon’s historical trace_callMany read the next block’s system writes at block 55; #24293 fixed it on main and the development build now agrees. The stricter Harmonized milestone is also blocked by schema-invalid beacon-call-55 responses from Besu and Nethermind 2.0.0: the beacon-roots contract REVERTs and both omit the REVERT frame result that H09 requires; Nethermind’s development build keeps it since #13981. This records agreement on the checked block boundary, not complete system-operation coverage or unanimous formal approval.

sources.label: Erigon #24056: read account state at the end of the requested block
Besu #10953: replay block pre-execution before tracing transactions

H29.note: Erigon, Nethermind (#13957), Reth and the Geth draft keep root precompile calls and omit nested zero-value precompile frames while keeping value-bearing ones. Besu has a partial fix open (#11360); Anvil nightly keeps nested zero-value frames in mined traces. This records direction from implementations, not unanimous formal approval.

H30.note: Every development build defaults omitted trace_filter bounds to latest against one head: Reth (#27411, released in 2.7.0), Erigon (#24341) and Nethermind (#13935) merged the change, and Besu and the Geth draft already matched. Erigon’s maintainer agreed to ship it without a deprecation period. This records direction from implementations, not unanimous formal approval.

H31.note: Erigon, Nethermind and Reth accept an omitted trace_callMany block and use latest, matching trace_call; Reth 2.7.0 is the first release to do so (#27410). Besu requires the block argument, with no submitted fix. This records direction from implementations, not unanimous formal approval.

H32.note: Converged on numeric and tag trace_filter bounds only: a block-hash string or EIP-1898 object as fromBlock or toBlock is rejected (-32602 recommended), as eth_getLogs range bounds reject them, and a single block is pinned by hash through H33’s blockHash member. Erigon (2026-09-29) and Nethermind (2026-09-30) asked for this contract publicly, which reverses the September 30 grandfathering of canonical hash endpoints. Pending, safe/finalized and single-view rules are unchanged. Reth and Besu have not answered; this is direction aligned rather than unanimous formal approval.

erigon.note: trace_filter should take the same bound types as eth_getLogs, so no block-hash or EIP-1898 range bounds; reviewing #24357 showed the cost of keeping them (the same block past the executed head is -32602 by number and -32000 by hash). Raised single-block selection by hash as a separate question (H33). The September 30 grandfathering revision was reversed back to this stricter contract, so the agreement applies again.

nethermind.note: Rejects hash range bounds (-32602) and wants a single block pinned through a trace_filter blockHash member instead, as eth_getLogs does.

H33.note: Converged on a canonical-only blockHash member for trace_filter, in the EIP-234 shape: mutually exclusive with non-null bounds (-32602 recommended), exactly the hashed block including [], and an error rather than [] or another block’s records for an unknown or noncanonical hash. Nethermind asked for this contract publicly and its development build implements it (#14111); Erigon raised the member publicly and privately supports canonical-only resolution. Reth and Besu have not answered. Serving side-chain blocks is out of scope. Direction aligned, not unanimous formal approval.

erigon.note: Raised the member publicly: without it no single call pins a block by hash and filters by address, and an empty numeric result is ambiguous after a reorg; proposed aligning trace_filter with eth_getLogs’ EIP-234 member and said either answer works for Erigon. Privately supports canonical-only hash resolution and reports that its existing eth_getLogs and trace_filter hash resolution is canonical-only. Together these cover the recommendation’s two choices, the member and canonical-only selection; no Erigon build implements the member yet.

sources.label: Erigon canonicality feedback

nethermind.note: Add a blockHash member to trace_filter and reject hash bounds (-32602); a non-null blockHash with fromBlock/toBlock is rejected, and an unknown or non-canonical hash returns an error, not [].
